name: Veldtmann Pressline Day Crew Full Kit
description:
A complete corponation-issued day shift uniform from Veldtmann Manufacturing. The core piece is a heavyweight charcoal synth-cotton coverall with a reinforced front zip and snap-over storm flap, stamped with the Veldtmann logo in faded white on the left chest and a sewn name patch on the right. The sleeves are cut wide at the right forearm to accommodate chrome prosthetics, with a magnetic closure cuff that seals clean around standard aug interfaces. Hi-vis orange reflective tape runs in twin horizontal bands across the chest and around both upper arms. Underneath sits a sweat-wicking thermal base layer in slate grey, visible at the collar. A rigid-shell hard hat in safety orange with a cracked brim that's been re-taped at the seam crowns the look.

The lower half features built-in knee pad channels with worn-in molded inserts, and the thighs carry three tool loops and a zip cargo pocket on the left leg reinforced with bar-tack stitching. Boots are Veldtmann Steelcap 7s — composite-toe, oil-resistant sole, black with orange heel striping that matches the coverall tape. Heavy-duty work gloves in charcoal nitrile-coated synth-leather hang clipped to a D-ring at the hip. The whole kit reads worn but maintained: clean at shift start, grimy by shift end, and built to survive both.
functionality: Full shift coverage with thermal base layer, aug-compatible sleeve cuff with magnetic closure, integrated knee protection, tool loops, cargo storage, steel-cap foot protection, hi-vis reflective banding for hazardous floor environments
what_it_says: This person clocks in, clocks out, and does not complain. The name patch means they are accountable to a corponation roster. The worn knee inserts and re-taped hard hat say they have been here long enough to break things and fix them. The maintained cleanliness says they have pride in the work even if not in the employer.
worn_by: industrial shift workers across Circuit-tier manufacturing plants
price_range: Φ 180–Φ 260 (subsidized at Φ 40–Φ 80 out of pocket for Veldtmann employees)
story_hooks: A character in this uniform is found somewhere they should not be — the Veldtmann logo places them precisely, but the shift log says they clocked out six hours ago.
The name patch belongs to someone else — a dead coworker whose identity the wearer has quietly assumed to keep drawing a paycheck.
A union organizer uses the uniform's corponation branding as cover to move through a rival facility unquestioned, until someone reads the name patch.

physical_description.visual_profile: A complete industrial work uniform that reads utilitarian and purposeful. The charcoal coverall dominates the silhouette with its wide-cut sleeves and reinforced front, creating a blocky, no-nonsense appearance. Hi-vis orange bands break the neutral palette horizontally across chest and arms, commanding visibility. The cracked hard hat and steel-toe boots anchor the look as serious protective gear. Overall impression: shift worker, machinery handler, union-adjacent corpo factory labor.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and deliberately oversized through the torso and sleeves to accommodate augmentations and layering. The right forearm features intentionally wider cut for chrome prosthetic clearance. Tapered at the ankle with reinforced ankle cuffs. Allows full range of motion and multiple layers underneath without binding.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight charcoal synth-cotton blend for the coverall; slate grey sweat-wicking thermal base layer; composite-toe boots with oil-resistant rubber sole; nitrile-coated synth-leather work gloves; rigid plastic hard hat shell.
physical_description.texture: Coverall fabric is sturdy and slightly stiff when new, softening with wear into a broken-in suppleness. Reflective tape creates smooth, slick tactile contrast. Knee pads show molded indentation from repeated use. Hard hat has a textured grip surface on the sides. Boot sole is slightly tacky, designed for grip on industrial floors.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey as dominant base. Safety orange hi-vis bands across chest and arms; orange heel striping on boots; orange hard hat. Slate grey thermal base layer visible at collar. Black boots with orange accents. Faded white Veldtmann logo on chest. Overall palette is industrial and high-contrast for visibility in low-light factory environments.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty friction-fit front zip on coverall with snap-over storm flap for weather protection. Magnetic closure cuff around right forearm to seal aug interfaces cleanly. Standard laces on boots. D-ring hip attachment for glove clip. Reinforced bar-tack stitching at stress points (cargo pocket, knee pad channels).
distinctive_features: Magnetic closure cuff sized for standard chrome prosthetic interfaces
Wide right forearm cut to accommodate cybernetic limbs
Built-in knee pad channels with molded inserts showing wear patterns
Twin hi-vis orange reflective bands for visibility
Sewn name patch on right chest (personalization slot)
Faded white Veldtmann Manufacturing logo stamped on left chest
Three tool loops and reinforced zip cargo pocket on left thigh
Cracked hard hat brim re-taped at seam
Steel-toe composite boots with orange heel striping
D-ring hip clip for work gloves
Sweat-wicking thermal base layer built into uniform system
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class). This is subsidized corpo-issued gear, not luxury, but not salvage. Veldtmann Manufacturing provides it to employees as part of their compensation structure. Quality is reliable and functional, not aspirational.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals factory worker, machine operator, or floor technician in a corpo manufacturing setting. Wearing full kit indicates shift-ready compliance. The worn condition suggests someone actively on the job, not office-bound. Augmentation accommodation suggests this person has integrated chrome, marking them as someone who's invested in staying employable in industrial work. Suggests GLMZ lower-tier manufacturing sector, possibly auto, parts, or heavy goods assembly.
physical_description.condition_typical: Coverall arrives pristine from Veldtmann supply but within one month shows weathering: stains that don't fully wash out, minor fraying at edges, faded logos. Knee pads develop shine marks from repeated kneeling. Hard hat accumulates micro-scratches and tape becomes discolored. Boots retain structural integrity but develop scuff patterns and salt stains. Gloves show oil residue and minor punctures. The garment is maintained but not precious — functional wear is expected and accepted.
